newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 7.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Thais hail Clinton win but expect tough stance. Thailand welcomed the re-election of U.S. President Bill Clinton yesterday but expects him to adopt a more aggressive policy of market access during the forthcoming meeting of leaders of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.

Top Thai officials also hope that Clinton's re-election will result in closer bilateral ties and a stronger U.S. role in Asia. Clinton is due for a state visit to Thailand on November 25. (BANGKOK POST)

- New Aspiration Party (NAP) under attack as teachers gain holiday. The education ministry yesterday announced an unprecedented holiday for state-run schools the day after the general election, as the Democrat Party reiterated accusations that the NAP was abusing its hold on the education portfolio to improperly garner support from teachers. Education Permanent Secretary Surat Silapa-anan said all schools run by the ministry will be closed on Monday, November 18, so teachers can go home to vote and not have to worry about their classes. (THE NATION)

- Police poll shows that two parties are neck to neck ahead of Nov 17 election. The survey conducted by the police department shows that the New Aspiration Party and Democrat Party will have a close race in the election where both parties are expected to win about 120 seats. Chart Pattana will come in third with about some 50 seats, the poll showed. The margin of error in the survey is plus or minus 10 seats. (SIAM POST)

- Airlines want cargo strike compensation. Some airlines will ask Thai Airways Internatonal to compensate them for a two-day strike by the carrier's cargo employees. They claim the stoppage damaged their air freight services and customer confidence. All the strikers resumed work on Tuesday night after their representatives and Thai management compromised on three key points. THAI agreed to suspend its participation in setting up a new air cargo carrier until the pros and cons are studied and the findings considered by the cabinet. (BANGKOK POST)

- Loan restructuring to keep realty afloat. The Bank of Thailand, after finding no better short-term solutions to revive the ailing property market, has agreed to allow financial institutions to restructure property loans in a bid to give more breathing room to cash strapped developers. (THE NATION)
